examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Dimension of the Product of Two Matrices
examples.problem:
Let
$[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 \\ -2 & 9\end{aligned}]$
and
$[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & 8\end{aligned}]$
What are the dimensions of $BA?$
examples.worked_solution:
We notice that $A$ is a $4 \times 2$ matrix and $B$ is a $2 \times 4$ matrix. 

There are $4$ columns in $B$ and $4$ rows in $A.$ Since the number of columns in $B$ equals the number of rows in $A,$ the matrices $B$ and $A$ are conformable for multiplication. 

The product $BA$ has dimensions $2 \times 2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\underset{\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \times \color{green}{\fbox{4}}}{B} \underset{\color{green}\checkmark}{\times} \underset{{\color{green}\fbox{4}} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2}}{A} = 
	\underset{\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2}}{BA}
$$

feedback.problem: Suppose $U$ is a $2\times 3$ matrix and $V$ is a $5\times 2$ matrix. What are the dimensions of $VU?$
feedback.worked_solution:
There are $2$ columns in $V$ and $2$ rows in $U.$ Since the number of columns in $V$ equals the number of rows in $U,$ the matrices $V$ and $U$ are conformable for multiplication, and $VU$ is a $5\times 3$ matrix:

$$
{V}_{5\times \boxed{\text{2}}}{\times }_{✓}{U}_{\boxed{\text{2}}\times 3}={VU}_{5\times 3}
$$
